newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court denies appeals in United Way case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court denies appeals in United Way case.

text.p: The Supreme Court Tuesday let stand the convictions of former United Way of America president William Aramony and former chief financial officer Thomas Merlo on conspiracy, fraud and tax charges.
The high court rejected appeals by Aramony, who headed the nationwide charity for 22 years until 1992, and Merlo, a close friend of Aramony and a certified public accountant.

Aramony, Merlo and another associate were convicted on charges of bilking the charity organisation out of more than $1 million and using United Way money for their own personal gain from the mid-1980s until the early 1990s.
According to testimony, Aramony used the charity's money to underwrite his relationships with various women, providing them with expensive trips and gifts.
After the trial in 1995 in federal court in Alexandria, Virginia, Aramony, 68, was sentenced to seven years in prison while Merlo received a prison term of 4-1/2 years.
A U.S. appeals court last year upheld convictions on 23 of 25 charges for Aramony and 14 of 17 charges for Merlo.

In the Supreme Court appeals, Aramony and Merlo argued the judge improperly instructed the jury on co-conspirator liability and should have held an evidentiary hearing on certain attorney-privilege claims involving an internal United Way investigation.
But the high court sided with the Justice Department in denying the appeals without any comment or dissent.
